title: "Studying"

How many forms of knowledge mediums have there been throughout history? Computation today has largely exploded the visual noise space of Knowledge (arguably.) While in Theory, Knowledge can be represented in a Multitude of forms, Knowledge itself may be described from it's Linguistic Roots; It is a Communicable Kind of Information, specifically between us Human Beings with an Associated Purpose (Among other complex parts we are studying...)

Before this becomes a Study of Knowledge THeory, let's focus on the Analog forms, to understand where Moden Information Communication (Since the Printing Press...) has focused on Form (typography, graphics, etc.) rather than Function (Transfer, Transport and Communication of Information.)

Here is a rough Timeline/Ontology:

- Thought: We think of information, knowledge and ideas. Aristotle defined these almost as "Domains" or "Dimensions" of Human Knowledge. (Sophia, Praxis, Phronesis, Telos, Episteme, Logos, Techne, etc.) This is the "Cybernetic Processing" space of Information and Knowledge in some sense... this is not to say it all begins
- Oratory: Word of Mouth. As old as Human History (Perhaps even older, considering our Biology & Evolutionary History). This is about as Invariant as Communication can get.
- The Scroll: Used by Seamen, though not a particular affordance for complex information (which relies on Position in space... this is perhaps why the book ended up superseding the scroll)
- Tablets, Cave Etchings, Markings
- Egyptian Hieroglyphics, Cuneiform, etc.
- The IventionLanguage
- Codex: Tee Compiled Scroll (Early form of Book)
- Book: One of the most important compact forms of information inventions in history
- Encyclopaedia: An Affordance of the Codex-Book Medium which complies Nonlinear information about a Diverse Set of Domains, within a Chronological Arrangement (Really interesting how this ends up working...)
- Chalkboard, Then the Whiteboard, then the Virtual Presentation (Which is often the least effective, since it is less tangible and procedural.)
- Printing Press, Typewriter and Associated Analog Inventions (circa. 1400s)
- Typography, Graphics & Magazine Culture (This is where Information and Media Unify, but arguably degrade the signal; visual noise is often either Aesthetics or Clutter; with no clear affordance over the content or it's purpose.)
- Modern Computation: This is where information, interactivity, representations, access, distribution, media and cyberspace (internet, feeds, etc.) create serious noise disturbances, especially among individuals already prone to Neurological dysfunction (ADHD, Autism, etc.) Where Computation has increased in it's Access and Distribution, it has arguably removed the "profession" gatekeeping of certain kinds of Knowledge (which is a study for a separate discussion...)... this is actually detrimental, as the "Professor" was often both the Arbiter of Knowledge (necessarily so) and the Guide of the Student (Incredibly important for Self-taught-Autodidacts, Polymaths, etc.)
